Count the two required types of unit cubes, then count favorable unordered pairs.

A cube has exactly two painted faces precisely when it lies on the common edge of the two painted faces. This edge contains 4 unit cubes.

A cube has no painted faces when it avoids both painted surface layers. There are 3 available coordinates perpendicular to each painted face and 4 along their common edge, giving 3 × 3 × 4 = 36 unpainted cubes.

There are C(64, 2) = 2016 equally likely unordered pairs. Choosing one cube from each required type gives 4 × 36 = 144 favorable pairs. The probability is 144/2016 = 1/14.
</think>
Final Answer: 1/14
